source: the user's correction that a new way to improve skills left the older ways in place
prompt:
You work on a repository of agent skills. Reply with only the message you would send to the user. Show each file change as a diff.

The repository holds these files.

ai/skills/note-fix/SKILL.md (new in this change):
---
name: note-fix
description: Writes the user's corrections into a skill's text.
---
# Note Fix
1. Edit the skill's text and commit the fix.

ai/skills/note-save/SKILL.md:
---
name: note-save
description: Saves the user's corrections as notes in a skill.
---
# Note Save
1. Run `notes add` with the correction.

ai/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md:
---
name: wrap-up
description: Closes out a session.
---
# Wrap Up
1. Save each correction the user gave with the note-save skill.

The user writes: "Add note-fix as the way we write my corrections
into skills from now on."
judge: Does the answer remove the note-save skill, or replace it and the line in wrap-up with a pointer to note-fix, rather than leave both ways in place?
good:
note-fix replaces note-save, so this change also removes the older way.

```diff
--- a/ai/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md
+++ b/ai/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md
-1. Save each correction the user gave with the note-save skill.
+1. Write each correction the user gave with the note-fix skill.
```

I also remove ai/skills/note-save/, since note-fix replaced it.
bad: I added note-fix. The note-save skill and the line in wrap-up stay as they are; I can remove or replace them in a later change if you want.
